definitions.explanation: The part of a roof that projects beyond the wall of a building.

examples.japanese: {軒|のき}から{雨|あま}だれが{落|お}ちている。
examples.english: Raindrops are falling from the eaves.

examples.japanese: {軒下|のきした}で{雨宿|あまやど}りをした。
examples.english: I took shelter from the rain under the eaves.

examples.japanese: {軒|のき}の{深|ふか}い{日本家屋|にほんかおく}は{夏|なつ}{涼|すず}しい。
examples.english: Traditional Japanese houses with deep eaves are cool in summer.

notes:
{軒|のき} refers to the overhanging edge of a roof. Deep eaves are a characteristic feature of traditional Japanese architecture.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {軒下|のきした} (under the eaves)
- {軒先|のきさき} (edge of the eaves, front of a shop)
- {軒|のき}を{連|つら}ねる (to stand in a row, of houses/shops)
- {雨宿|あまやど}り (taking shelter from rain)

ARCHITECTURAL NOTE:
Deep {軒|のき} in traditional Japanese architecture serve to shade interiors from summer sun while allowing winter sunlight to enter.

NOTE: {軒|けん} is also a counter for houses/buildings.
